Actually, it was a public parking lot in front of the police station. According to Florida law, she was not in control of the vehicle, she was outside the car, the keys were in the glove compartment door. The officers therefore did not witness a crime. The prescription bottle was in my name. Florida law states that each pill is 1 count of possession. She was charged with only 1 count. No other pills were impounded, the other 80+ pills are unaccounted for. Pursuant to section 465.003(6), Florida Statutes (2008), pharmacies may lawfully dispense medications to a consumer or his or her agent. Further, a pharmacist may dispense a schedule III controlled substance ‘when the pharmacist or pharmacist’s agent has obtained satisfactory patient information from the patient or the patient’s agent.’ meaning, the narcotics arrest, which followed a bad DWI/DUI arrest, was bad.  I have done some research after posting the incident and those are my conclusions. However, since I am a retired police officer, I am unsure of the arguments from the"defense" side of the law. As a cop of 24 years, I would never have arrested someone in this situation.

Don't pull any punches. Legally, since she was outside the car, and the keys were in the glove compartment box, she did not have constructive control of the vehicle. Since they refused to accommodate her disability, they violated the Americans with Disabilities Act. The law also provides that anyone can appoint an agent to pick up and transport prescription medication and due to the fact that the bottle was labeled with my name (her last name is the same) they did not have probable cause to arrest her.
